mainTopic: How long a נבלה stays impure, why a חררת דם is pure, brine mixed with water, nursing animals, and רב's rule for deciding the הלכה in this פרק
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבי ירמיה, and the גמרא admits it is a real difficulty. It then studies the dispute itself. בר פדא says severe טומאה lasts only while the item is fit for a גר, and light טומאה lasts while it is fit for a dog. רבי יוחנן says both kinds last while it is fit for a dog, and the two argue over how to read the פסוק about נבלה. Next the גמרא explains why a חררת דם does not make things impure: it is because of ביטול ברוב, since it was once fit to eat as part of its mother. A side discussion explains why pure ציר becomes impure when any water falls in, with two answers about how much water an עם הארץ adds. A new משנה of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that we do not worry that a nursing animal is feeding another animal's young. Finally רב rules that the הלכה follows the whole פרק except where there is a dispute. רב ששת challenges what this ruling adds, and the גמרא answers that it means a disagreement found only in a ברייתא does not count. A new question about this rule then begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן's view: the mass is still fit for a dog
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, every kind of טומאה lasts as long as the item is fit for a dog. The חררת דם is fit for a dog, so why should it not make things impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the view that both kinds of impurity last until the item is unfit for a dog, there is a problem: this mass is fit for a dog!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an attack on רבי ירמיה's explanation of why the blood mass does not make things impure. It uses רבי יוחנן's rule to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה's explanation only works if the item must be fit for a person (a גר) to stay impure. רבי יוחנן says that fit for a dog is enough. A blood mass is fit for a dog, so under רבי יוחנן it should still be impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one (both kinds of impurity)
Until it is unfit for a dog

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ עַד לְכֶלֶב,
phrases.english: Both this one and that one last until it is unfit for a dog,
but this mass is fit for a dog!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about רבי ירמיה's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's explanation of why the חררת דם is not impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוחנן, being fit for a dog is enough to keep an item impure, and this mass is fit for a dog.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the question is a real difficulty and gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the challenge by saying "קשיא". The question stays open and nobody answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "קשיא" means the problem is acknowledged but the opinion is not formally thrown out. רבי ירמיה's explanation is left with an unanswered difficulty under רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the challenge from step 1 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under רבי יוחנן's view, רבי ירמיה's explanation remains difficult.

steps.title: בר פדא: severe impurity until fit for a גר, light impurity until fit for a dog
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא splits the rule. Severe impurity ends once the item is unfit for a גר, while light impurity lasts until it is unfit even for a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the main point itself. בר פדא says: severe impurity lasts until the item is unfit for a גר, and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The word "גופא" signals that the גמרא is now going back to study, on its own, the dispute it just relied on. בר פדא gives his rule first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Severe טומאה, like נבלה, needs a higher standard to stay in force: the item must still be food a person (a גר תושב) would eat. Light טומאה stays as long as even a dog would eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself (a fresh look at a quoted statement)
Here, a גר תושב (a non-Jew living in the land who may eat נבלה)

phrases.english: Now to the matter itself:
בר פדא says:
Severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a גר,
and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a separate look at the dispute that step 1 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Severe impurity lasts until the item is unfit for a גר; light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both kinds last until unfit for a dog
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and uses one standard for both kinds of impurity: fit for a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: both this one and that one last until the item is unfit for a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing view. רבי יוחנן makes no distinction between severe and light impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, even severe impurity like נבלה stays in force as long as a dog would still eat the item. This is the rule that caused the problem in step 1.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן says:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ עַד לְכֶלֶב.
phrases.english: Both this one and that one last until it is unfit for a dog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side to בר פדא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both severe and light impurity last until the item is unfit for a dog.

steps.title: What is בר פדא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind בר פדא's stricter standard for severe impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for בר פדא's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where בר פדא gets his special "fit for a גר" standard. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's single standard needs no special source. בר פדא's distinction does need one, so the גמרא asks for it.

phrases.english: What is the reason of בר פדא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion given in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for limiting severe impurity to items fit for a גר

steps.title: The פסוק: only what is fit for a גר is called נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links נבלה to giving it to a גר. So only meat a גר could eat counts as נבלה for impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "You shall not eat any carcass; to the גר..." What is fit for a גר is called a carcass, and what is not fit for a גר is not called a carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. Because the תורה describes נבלה as something you can give to a גר, בר פדא learns that something no גר would eat is no longer נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition of נבלה is tied to being edible for a person. Once the meat is too spoiled for a גר, it loses the name נבלה, and with it the severe impurity of נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה; it carries severe impurity

phrases.english: As it is written:
"You shall not eat any carcass; to the גר..."
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21. The rest of the פסוק says you may give it to the גר living among you.

phrases.english: What is fit for a גר is called "carcass,"
and what is not fit for a גר is not called "carcass."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כׇל נְבֵלָה לְגֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק describes נבלה as fit to give to a גר, so only what a גר could eat is נבלה.

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק: meat that spoiled from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as excluding only a carcass that was rotten from the very beginning, not one that rotted later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יוחנן)? He uses the פסוק to exclude a case where the carcass was spoiled from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן does with בר פדא's פסוק, and answers right away. He uses it for a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the פסוק teaches only that meat already spoiled at the moment the animal died never becomes נבלה. Meat that was fine at first and spoiled later stays impure as long as a dog would eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (how does the other opinion deal with this?)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רבי יוחנן: what does he do with this פסוק?

phrases.english: It comes to exclude where it was spoiled from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק used in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק excludes only a carcass that was spoiled from the outset.

steps.title: בר פדא: spoiled-from-the-start meat needs no פסוק
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא answers that meat rotten from the start is just dust, so no פסוק is needed to exclude it. The פסוק must teach his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (בר פדא)? Meat spoiled from the start needs no פסוק to exclude it; it is just dust.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives בר פדא's reply. He rejects רבי יוחנן's use of the פסוק as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meat was never food, it is obviously not נבלה, so the תורה would not need to say so. The פסוק must therefore teach something new: a carcass that later becomes unfit for a גר stops being נבלה.
steps.whatToRemember: בר פדא: severe impurity lasts until the item is unfit for a גר, based on the פסוק. רבי יוחנן: both kinds last until it is unfit for a dog; the פסוק excludes only meat spoiled from the start.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now it means בר פדא: how does he answer רבי יוחנן's reading?

phrases.aramaic: הִסְרִיחָה מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי,
phrases.english: Spoiled from the start needs no פסוק to exclude it,
it is mere dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? הִסְרִיחָה מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בר פדא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's reading from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוחנן's use of the פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Meat spoiled from the start is obviously not food, so a פסוק to exclude it would be unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה: a blood mass is buried and frees the animal from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: a large animal that discharged a חררת דם must bury it, and the animal's later offspring will not count as a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, a large animal that discharged a mass of blood must have it buried, and the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the משנה about the blood mass. This sets up the next statements about whether that mass makes things impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood mass counts as a birth, so it opens the womb and frees later offspring from בכורה. It is buried, just in case it is a בכור.

phrases.english: We learned:
רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:
A large animal that discharged a mass of blood,
that mass must be buried,
and the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the חררת דם case that the earlier discussion was about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood mass is buried, and the mother is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: רבי חייא: the blood mass does not make things impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that the חררת דם does not make things impure, neither by touching nor by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא teaches: it does not make things impure, neither by touching nor by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא about the blood mass. Although it is treated as a birth, it does not carry נבלה impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a surprising result: an item treated seriously enough to be buried still has no impurity. The next step gives the reason.

phrases.english: And רבי חייא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.english: It does not make things impure, neither by touching nor by carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a law about impurity to the case of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חררת דם does not make things impure by touching or by carrying.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: nullified in the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the חכמים ruled the mass is not impure because of ביטול ברוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: they addressed it because of nullification in a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the reason for רבי חייא's ruling: the mass is not impure because of ביטול ברוב. This explanation sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever could make the mass impure is outnumbered by the majority, so it is cancelled out. Note that this is a different reason from רבי ירמיה's "unfit for a גר" reason, which ran into trouble under רבי יוחנן's own view in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: They addressed it (the reason the חכמים ruled this way)

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:
Because of nullification in a majority did they address it.
phrases.notes: Literally "they touched it"; here it means this is the reason the חכמים ruled it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל בְּרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי חייא's ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood mass is not impure because of ביטול ברוב.

steps.title: Why need majority? The mass was never fit to eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: why rely on ביטול ברוב when the mass was never fit to eat at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why say the reason is ביטול ברוב? We could get the same result because the mass is not fit to eat at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the reason רבי יוחנן gave in Step 11. It suggests a simpler reason why the חררת דם is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the mass is pure because of ביטול ברוב. The גמרא says there is an easier reason: the mass was never fit to eat, so it should not carry the טומאה of a נבלה anyway. So why bring in ביטול ברוב?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Why pick this reason?
I could get it from (an easier reason)

phrases.english: Why specifically because of nullification by the majority?
Let me derive it from the fact that it is not fit at all!
phrases.notes: "Not fit" means not fit to eat, so it should never have the טומאה of a נבלה in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי יוחנן gave in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason of ביטול ברוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler reason, that the mass was never fit to eat, should be enough. So the reason of majority seems unneeded.

steps.title: It was once fit through its mother
steps.stepSummary: The mass was fit at first as part of its mother, so we do need ביטול ברוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too was fit at the start, as part of its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The mass did have a time when it was fit to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before it came out, the mass was inside the mother. If the mother had been slaughtered then, it could have been eaten along with her. Since it was once fit, the 'never fit' reason does not work, so רבי יוחנן needed ביטול ברוב.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of its mother, as part of its mother

phrases.english: This too was fit at the start
by way of its mother.
phrases.notes: Had the mother been slaughtered before it came out, it would have been edible with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי אִיתְחֲזִי מֵעִיקָּרָא אַגַּב אִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case does not match the challenger's assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mass was never fit to eat, so ביטול ברוב is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mass was fit at first through its mother, so only ביטול ברוב explains why it is pure.
steps.whatToRemember: The חררת דם is pure because of ביטול ברוב. The 'never fit' reason does not work, since it was once fit as part of its mother.

steps.title: Pure brine that water fell into
steps.stepSummary: A משנה: pure ציר that any amount of water fell into becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: pure brine that any amount of water fell into is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from somewhere else. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a tiny bit of water makes the pure ציר impure. That seems strange, since a little water should not matter. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Brine, the salty liquid from fish

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מכשירין 6:3.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Pure brine into which there fell
any amount of water is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about mixtures, linked to the idea of ביטול ברוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pure ציר that any amount of water falls into becomes impure.

steps.title: עמי הארץ are suspected of adding half water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the משנה shows that עמי הארץ are suspected of mixing half water into brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This shows that עמי הארץ are suspected of mixing half water into the brine.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא explains why a tiny bit of water makes the brine impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ may already have mixed water into the brine, up to half. The water of an עם הארץ is impure. While it is not more than the brine, it is cancelled out. When more water falls in, the water is no longer outweighed, so the whole mixture becomes impure.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are not careful about טומאה and טהרה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
This is to say
that amei ha'aretz are suspected
of mixing half water into the brine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמי הארץ are suspected of mixing half water into brine, so added water makes the whole mixture impure.

steps.title: Why exactly half? Less than half should work too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן said half, since even less than half would lead to the same result.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need half? Even with less than half too! This small amount makes it half, and half is not cancelled out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the exact wording of רב נחמן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say the עם הארץ added a bit less than half. The small amount of water that fell in brings it up to half. Half is not cancelled out by the other half, so it would be impure anyway. So why did רב נחמן say exactly half?
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word בְּצִיר means 'less than.' It is not the word צִיר, 'brine,' even though they look alike.

phrases.english: But why do I need half?
Even less than half too!
And this tiny amount makes it half,
and half is not cancelled out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'half' in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word מחצה in רב נחמן's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Less than half plus a tiny amount equals half, and half is not cancelled out. So 'exactly half' seems too specific.

steps.title: Read it as up to half
steps.stepSummary: First answer: change the wording to 'up to half.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: up to half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer by adjusting the wording of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן did not mean exactly half. He meant the עם הארץ adds water up to just under half. Then the tiny amount that falls in brings it to half, and half is not cancelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to half, just under half

phrases.english: Say: up to half.
phrases.notes: He means just under half. The water that falls in then brings it up to half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן meant exactly half water.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן meant up to just under half water.

steps.title: Two rabbinic rules: only a majority of water was made impure
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: both laws here are rabbinic, and the חכמים made it impure only when water is the majority, not at half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: the טומאה of an עם הארץ is rabbinic, and the טומאה of liquids is rabbinic. The חכמים made a rule for a majority, but for half and half the חכמים did not make a rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that keeps the word 'half' as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here two rabbinic rules are stacked together, so the חכמים were more lenient. They called the mixture impure only when the water is the majority. With exactly half water already in, the tiny bit that falls in makes the water the majority, so 'half' is the right word.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (a second answer)
From the חכמים, not from the תורה
They made a rule, they decreed

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: either 'half' means just under half, or the חכמים made the mixture impure only when water is the majority, because both rules here are rabbinic.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
the impurity of an am ha'aretz is rabbinic,
the impurity of liquids is rabbinic.
For a majority, the Rabbis decreed,

phrases.aramaic: בְּפַלְגָא וּפַלְגָא לָא גְּזַרוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: for half and half, the Rabbis did not decree about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: טוּמְאַת עַם הָאָרֶץ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 16 that keeps the word 'half.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the scope of the rabbinic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Half and half should already be impure, so 'half' is too specific.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since both rules are rabbinic, the חכמים made it impure only when water is the majority. So exactly half is needed, and the added water makes it the majority.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when two rabbinic rules stack together, the חכמים may set a more lenient limit.

steps.title: New משנה: no worry that a nursing animal feeds another's young
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: one who buys a nursing animal from a גוי, or sees nursing animals in his flock, does not need to worry that one nurses another's baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One who buys a nursing animal from a גוי does not worry that it was nursing another animal's baby. If he goes into his flock and sees first-time mothers nursing and other mothers nursing, he does not worry that one's baby went to the other, or the other's baby went to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that we trust what we see: a nursing animal is nursing its own baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying from a גוי, a nursing animal is treated as having already given birth. In one's own flock, we do not suspect that babies switched mothers. This matters for knowing which animal gave birth and which offspring count as a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Nursing, giving milk to a baby
We do not worry about it
Animals that gave birth for the first time

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who buys a nursing animal from a gentile,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל אַחֶרֶת הָיָה.
phrases.english: we do not worry that perhaps it was another animal's young.
If he went into his flock and saw
the first-time mothers nursing,
and those that are not first-time mothers nursing,
we do not worry

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ,
phrases.english: that perhaps this one's young came over to that one,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ.
phrases.english: or that perhaps that one's young came over to this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מְנִיקָה מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We assume a nursing animal is nursing its own young. We do not worry that it nurses another animal's baby, either when buying from a גוי or within one's own flock.

steps.title: רב's ruling: the הלכה follows the whole פרק except where there is a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: the הלכה follows everything in this פרק, except places where a מחלוקת is recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows this whole chapter, except where there is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a general ruling from רב about the whole פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is saying that the unattributed rulings of this פרק are the final הלכה. The only exception is wherever the משנה itself records a disagreement. The rest of the סוגיא will test what this ruling actually adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that follows the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Nachman said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows our whole chapter,
phrases.notes: He means the הלכה follows the rulings stated without a name attached.

phrases.english: except where there is a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הִלְכְתָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ פִּירְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of nursing animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows all the rulings in this פרק except where a dispute is recorded.

steps.title: רב ששת questions רב's ruling, starting with the first משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says רב must have been dozing, since it is unclear what the ruling adds. It cannot refer to the first משנה, because רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: I say רב was dozing or sleeping when he said this teaching! Which ruling could it refer to? If you say the first משנה, רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא disagree there!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב's statement and starts testing which ruling in the פרק it could be talking about. He rules out the first משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general ruling should teach something new. The first משנה has a recorded dispute, so רב's own words already exclude it. רב ששת is setting up a search through the whole פרק.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not insulting רב. He is saying that, as far as he can see, the statement adds nothing.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
I say that while dozing and lying asleep
Rav said this teaching!
About which ruling?
If you say about the first mishna,
they clearly disagree there:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא כִּי נָיֵים וְשָׁכֵיב רַב אָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling must teach something new. The first משנה has a dispute, so the ruling does not apply to it.

steps.title: Not רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, whose rulings are already accepted
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רב meant the ruling of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. But we already know the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב? But the teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is 'a קב and clean.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tries a second candidate and rules it out too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known principle that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teachings are few but reliable, so the הלכה follows him anyway. רב would not need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: The teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
Small in amount but pure, so always followed

phrases.english: Rather, about Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?
The teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov is
'a kav and clean.'
phrases.notes: A קב is a small measure: his teachings are few but completely reliable, so the הלכה already follows him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב ששת's search with a second candidate.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying רב's ruling to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying it would be unnecessary, since the הלכה already follows him.

steps.title: Not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, since a ברייתא disagrees with him
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רב meant רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling about nursing animals. But a ברייתא records someone who disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? Someone clearly disagrees with him in a ברייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tries a third candidate, the ruling from step 19, and rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no dispute in the משנה itself, but a ברייתא brings an opposing view. רב ששת assumes this counts as a dispute, so רב's rule would exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Rather, about Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
Someone clearly disagrees in a baraita!
phrases.notes: This is his ruling about nursing animals from step 19.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִפְלָג פְּלִיג בְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third candidate in the search.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying רב's ruling to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא records a dispute, so it falls under 'except where there is a dispute.'

steps.title: Not רבי יוסי בן המשולם, since רב already ruled like him
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רב meant רבי יוסי בן המשולם. But רב already said elsewhere that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to רבי יוסי בן המשולם? But רב already said this once, for רב said: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tries a fourth candidate and rules it out because it would be a repeat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב already gave a separate ruling following רבי יוסי בן המשולם. He would not need to say the same thing a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose ruling appears in the next משנה

phrases.english: Rather, about Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam?
But Rav already said this one time,
for Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם הָא אָמַר רַב חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth candidate in the search.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying רב's ruling to רבי יוסי בן המשולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would repeat a ruling רב already gave.

steps.title: Not the hair of a blemished בכור, which is disputed
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רב meant the case of hair from a blemished בכור. But עקביא בן מהללאל and the רבנן argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the hair of a blemished animal? עקביא בן מהללאל and the רבנן clearly disagree there!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tries a last candidate and rules it out. This finishes his challenge, leaving no ruling for רב's statement to refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה has a recorded dispute, so רב's own words exclude it. Every option has now failed, which puts the question to the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Hair of a בכור with a blemish
A תנא who disagrees with the רבנן in that משנה

phrases.english: Rather, about the hair of a blemished animal?
They clearly disagree there:
Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַשְּׂעַר בַּעַל מוּם מִיפְלָג פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final candidate. It completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying רב's ruling to the hair of a blemished בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה records a dispute, so the ruling would not apply.

steps.title: Answer: רב meant רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because a ברייתא's disagreement does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב was talking about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. His new point is that a dispute found only in a ברייתא is not treated as a dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רב teaches us this: a ברייתא does not count as a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by going back to the third candidate and showing what new point he is making.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת rejected this option because a ברייתא disagrees. The answer turns that objection into רב's actual lesson. When the משנה states a ruling without dispute, an opposing view found only in a ברייתא does not stop us from following the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really, going back to an earlier option
This is what he teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It teaches that if a משנה states a ruling with no dispute, a disagreeing view in a ברייתא does not count as a 'dispute.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a rule for deciding הלכה: the משנה's undisputed ruling stands even when a ברייתא disagrees.

phrases.english: Actually, it is about Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and this is what he teaches us:
that a baraita is not a dispute.
phrases.notes: He means an opposing view found only in a ברייתא does not count as a real dispute against the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge (steps 21-25) by going back to the candidate from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the term 'dispute' in רב's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A disagreement in a ברייתא counts as a dispute, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would be excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a dispute in the משנה itself counts. The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge from רב's general rule for the chapter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that רב said the הלכה follows the whole פרק except where there is a dispute. This prepares a challenge to the need for his specific ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since רב said: the הלכה follows our entire chapter, except where there is a dispute,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It reminds us of a general rule רב gave for this whole פרק, and the rest of the question comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gave a blanket rule: whatever this פרק teaches without an argument is the הלכה. If that general rule already covers a case, a separate specific ruling from רב looks unneeded. This line lays down the general rule so the גמרא can ask what the specific ruling adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / once it is so that. This opens an argument built on something already known.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete statement or ruling. It is only the first half of a question, and the challenge itself comes next.

phrases.english: And since רב said:
the halakha follows our entire chapter
phrases.notes: He means the cases the משנה states without anyone arguing.

phrases.english: except where there is a dispute,
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. The question finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 26 settled what רב's general rule refers to, the גמרא uses that general rule to question why רב also needed his separate ruling following רבי יוסי בן המשולם (step 24).
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב's separate ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם (step 24).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב already ruled that the הלכה follows everything in the פרק except where there is a dispute, his separate ruling following רבי יוסי בן המשולם looks redundant. This line sets up that general rule as the basis of the challenge.
